paper_summary: Majlinger and Orbulov produced hybrid aluminium matrix syntactic foams (ASFs) by inert-gas (Ar, 400 kPa) pressure infiltration of Al99.5 (Al1050) or near-eutectic AlSi12 (Al4047) melt into randomly close-packed beds (~64 vol%) of hollow spheres: large ceramic Globocer (GC, 1450 um, 60 um wall, 0.816 g/cm3), large metallic Globomet (GM, 0.4 g/cm3) and small ceramic E-sphere SLG (130 um, 6 um wall, 0.637 g/cm3), in GM/GC ratios varied in 20 vol% steps and in an SLG-GC bimodal blend. SEM/EDS showed near-complete infiltration (uninfiltrated void content well below 3%) and thin interface layers under 10 um. Quasi-static compression (DIN 50134, 0.01 1/s, H/D = 1.5) gave compressive strengths from 65 MPa (60GM-40GC) up to 180 MPa (AlSi12-SLG); compressive strength and structural stiffness rose with GC content while fracture strain fell, and the small-sphere SLG foams gave the highest strength and fracture strain at the lowest density.

processing.matrix_name: AlSi12 (Al4047) near-eutectic Al-Si casting alloy; measured 12.830 wt% Si, 0.127 wt% Fe, 0.002 wt% Cu, 0.005 wt% Mn, 0.010 wt% Mg, 0.007 wt% Zn, balance Al
processing.particle_grade: Globomet (GM) metallic hollow spheres, Hollomet GmbH; density 0.4 g/cm3, average diameter similar to GC (1450 um) but with lower wall thickness. 100 vol% GM of the sphere fraction.

structure.microstructure_notes: Uninfiltrated void content between the hollow spheres remained well below 3% for all ASFs (upper bound only, not a measured value). Interface layer with the AlSi12 matrix ~7 um for GM spheres. Molten AlSi12 dissolves Fe from the GM sphere walls, so most broken/infiltrated spheres were GM grade. These ASFs behaved like conventional metallic foams: no pronounced compressive strength peak, long slowly rising plateau, fully plastic deformation.

extraction_notes:
Ten records, one per row of Table 1 (all at H/D = 1.5, quasi-static compression at 0.01 1/s). Decimal commas in Table 1 were read as decimal points (e.g. '1,64' -> 1.64; '5,0' -> 5.0%).

Field mapping: sigma_c (compressive strength, first stress peak) -> strength_mpa; S (structural stiffness, initial slope of the stress-strain curve, MPa) -> modulus_mpa - note this is a structural stiffness per DIN 50134, not a true Young's modulus, and the paper shows it varies with the H/D aspect ratio; the 'C (%)' column is the fracture strain eps_c at sigma_c defined in the text, converted from percent to a fraction (e.g. 5.0% -> 0.05).

Energy absorption is NOT filled in. Table 1 gives W at eps=25% with the printed unit 'Jm-3'; the magnitudes (1200-5000) are inconsistent with that unit by several orders of magnitude for foams of 65-180 MPa strength, so the unit is very likely a typo (kJ/m3 or MJ/m3 was probably intended). Rather than guess a conversion, energy_absorption_mj_m3 is left null. The raw tabulated values are: 100GM-0GC 1200; 80GM-20GC 1550; 60GM-40GC 1500; 40GM-60GC 1400; 20GM-80GC 1650; AlSi12-0GM-100GC 1650 (and 2700 at eps=50%); Al99.5-0GM-100GC 2800*; AlSi12-SLG 5000*; Al99.5-SLG 4000*; AlSi12-SLG-GC 2300*, where * denotes values that correspond to eps=50% rather than 25%.

AlSi12-100GM-0GC has no compressive strength or fracture strain ('n.a.' in Table 1) because pure GM-reinforced foams show no pronounced strength peak; those fields are null.

Particle type for hybrid GM/GC blends: the schema allows a single particle type, so the majority sphere fraction was used - metal_hollow for 100GM, 80GM-20GC and 60GM-40GC; ceramic_hollow for 40GM-60GC, 20GM-80GC and 100GC. The actual blend ratio is always stated in sample_label and particle_grade. The SLG-GC record is bimodal ceramic and the SLG:GC ratio is never given numerically in the paper.

particle_wall_thickness_ratio (eta = inner/outer radius) is not reported by the authors; for the pure-GC records it was computed as (725-60)/725 = 0.917 and for the pure-SLG records as (65-6)/65 = 0.908 from the stated diameters and wall thicknesses. It is left null for hybrid blends and for GM (whose wall thickness is only described qualitatively as 'lower' than GC).

particle_volume_fraction = 0.64 for every record: 'The total amount of reinforcement was maintained at high level (~64 vol.%) that corresponds to randomly closed packed structure.'

matrix_porosity_fraction left null: the paper only gives the upper bound 'uninfiltrated void content between the hollow spheres remained well below 3%', not a measured value.

cure_or_process_temperature_c left null: the infiltration temperature is never stated numerically (only the 400 kPa argon pressure and the vacuum-assisted procedure are given). Test temperature set to 25 C from 'The compression tests were performed ... at room temperature'.

Other data not extracted: Fig. 5 gives structural stiffness versus H/D ratio (1, 1.5, 2) and Fig. 4 gives stress-strain curves at H/D = 1, but numerical values for H/D = 1 and 2 are only readable off the plots, so no records were created for those aspect ratios. Hollow-sphere single-particle fracture forces (GC 22.1 +/- 1.18 N, GM 5.1 +/- 0.18 N) and interface layer thicknesses (7/5/5 um for GM/GC/SLG with AlSi12) have no schema field and are recorded in particle_grade / microstructure_notes.

Evidence quotes for Table 1 rows are reconstructed across the line-per-cell layout of the extracted text (the source file lists each table cell on its own line) and preserve the original decimal commas.
